findings.finding: Retry seam (sendWithRateLimitRetry/sendWith5xxRetry/sendOnce) refactored to return raw TelegramSendResult<JsonNode>; SentMessage mapping moved into send(). Lets answerCallbackQuery reuse the exact retry/deadline/429 loop without duplicating it. mapBodyToSentMessage stays on the content path only. Behavior-preserving — TelegramSenderTest and TelegramSenderSubscriberHookIT pass unchanged.
sendOnce now omits chat_id body key when chatId==null (ack path). Content sends always pass non-null chatId, so /sendMessage and /sendPhoto bodies are unchanged.

answerCallbackQuery wraps the whole ack path (findById + CONNECTED filter + decrypt + retry) in catch(RuntimeException) → scrub + WARN with greppable TELEGRAM_ANSWER_CALLBACK_FAILED. No audit event, no subscriber hook. Matches Decision 8 best-effort and the existing TELEGRAM_SENDER_SUBSCRIBER_HOOK_FAILED swallow-and-warn convention.

answerCallbackQuery re-derives attempts/deadline + repeats the findById+CONNECTED filter inline instead of going through send(). Intentional and documented in Javadoc: ack must bypass the audit/subscriber-hook pipeline that send() applies. Acceptable per task Details ("answerCallbackQuery is NOT content-send").
